text:
Recent evidence supports distinguishing relevance from personal choice. *Can LLM be a Personalized Judge?* (2024) finds personalized preference evaluation difficult even for human third-party annotators; inferred preferences should therefore remain distinct from users’ explicit choices. A 2025–2026 recommendation study reports stronger human alignment with richer metadata and longer histories, but this supports contextual relevance assessment, not reliable inference of immediate purchase intent or rejection motives. [Personalized judging study](https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.592/), [recommendation evaluation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.23312).

A defensible protocol, synthesized from this evidence: annotate immediate choice only from explicit feedback; label broad relevance, redundancy, explicit specification mismatch and insufficient information separately. Attach supporting title/description/history/feedback spans to each judgment. Treat repeated history items as observed repetition, without inferring ownership; establish compatibility mismatch only when both the requirement and conflicting specification are explicit. Otherwise abstain. Criteria-based relevance assessment provides a useful precedent for decomposing judgments, while a 2025 evidence-annotation protocol explicitly distinguishes topical relevance from sufficient support or refutation. These are methodological precedents, not a validated recommendation-rejection taxonomy. [Criteria-based judgments](https://www.cs.unh.edu/~dietz/papers/farzi2025criteria.pdf), [evidence annotation protocol](https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.968.pdf).

Validate automated proxies against a bounded, independently double-annotated sample spanning all four categories. Pilot the rubric, measure agreement before adjudication, and report per-label agreement, Cohen’s κ or Krippendorff’s α, uncertainty intervals, abstention coverage and proxy errors. JUDGE-BENCH (2025) finds judge performance inconsistent across and within tasks, making local validation essential. Keep these diagnostic outcomes separate from pinned macro validation HR@10; do not infer simulator traits. [JUDGE-BENCH](https://clp.ling.uni-potsdam.de/publications/Bavaresco-2025.pdf).
